settings.heading: We made coffee for the places we'd rather be.

settings.text: We buy direct from a handful of farms we visit each year. Smaller lots, fairer prices, and a list of names instead of a co-op number.
The coffee gets roasted in small batches in Brooklyn, ground the same week, and sealed into compostable filter sachets. Then it leaves the warehouse and shows up at your door.

settings.title: Boil.
settings.body: Fresh water, just off the boil. Around 200°F. A kettle whistle works fine.

settings.title: Drop.
settings.body: Place a sachet in your mug. Tag out, like tea. Don't squeeze it.

settings.title: Pour.
settings.body: Fill to the brim. The steam counts. Watch the bloom for ten seconds.

settings.title: Wait.
settings.body: Four minutes. Don't check your phone.

settings.quote: "You can drink coffee with two bars of signal, or no bars at all. The coffee doesn't care. Maybe you don't either."

settings.heading:
Compostable.
Not just recyclable.
settings.tag: 100% Plant-based filter · OK for your backyard compost
settings.body: The sachet is plant fiber and corn starch. The wrapper is uncoated kraft. The box is the box. Bury the whole thing in the garden and it'll be soil by spring.

settings.heading:
Resupply
the pack.
settings.body: The trip doesn't end. Subscribe and we ship the next round before you run out.
